revealWordProblem.title: Apply: A New Park
revealWordProblem.text:
Claire, a city horticulturist, is developing the new park shown to replace an old city lot. The center of the park will hold a koi pond covering 1,245 square feet. Eighty-five percent of the remaining space will be covered with grass seed. A 50-pound bag of grass seed covers up to 7,500 square feet, and one bale of straw covers about 500 square feet of seeded ground.
Choose a question to answer.
Question 1: How many bags of grass seed should be used to seed the park?
Question 2: How many bales of straw should be used to cover the grass seed?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: An overhead view of a parallelogram-shaped park with a koi pond, labeled 150 feet along the base and 108 feet for the perpendicular height.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The park is a parallelogram, so its area is base × height = 150 × 108 = 16,200 square feet. Take out the pond: 16,200 − 1,245 = 14,955 square feet remain. Eighty-five percent of that gets grass seed: 0.85 × 14,955 = 12,711.75 square feet. Question 1: 12,711.75 ÷ 7,500 = 1.7, and seed comes in whole bags, so she should buy 2 bags. Question 2: 12,711.75 ÷ 500 = 25.4, so she needs 26 bales of straw.

questions.stem: What is the area of a parallelogram with base 10 cm and height 7 cm?
choiceFeedback: Did you add? The formula multiplies base and height.
That label measures a distance along a line, but area describes the flat region a shape covers. Multiplying two lengths always produces square units.
hints: You know both the base (10 cm) and the height (7 cm) — this is a direct use of the parallelogram area formula.
Area of a parallelogram is A = base × height. Adding the two numbers gives perimeter-style thinking, not area.
Set up A = 10 × 7 and multiply. Label your result in square centimeters.
questions.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el área de un paralelogramo con base 10 cm y altura 7 cm?
hintsEs: Conoces tanto la base (10 cm) como la altura (7 cm): este es un uso directo de la fórmula del área del paralelogramo.
El área de un paralelogramo es A = base × altura. Sumar los dos números es pensar en perímetro, no en área.
Plantea A = 10 × 7 y multiplica. Escribe tu resultado en centímetros cuadrados.

questions.stem: A parallelogram has an area of 54 sq ft and a base of 9 ft. What is the height?
choiceFeedback: Work backwards: if A = b × h and A = 54, h = 54 ÷ 9.
54 + 9 is too large for the height.
hints: This time you're given the area (54 sq ft) and the base (9 ft) — the height is the missing piece.
Start from A = b × h. To undo a multiplication, divide: h = A ÷ b.
Write 54 = 9 × h, then divide 54 by 9 to find the height in feet.
questions.stemEs: Un paralelogramo tiene un área de 54 pies cuadrados y una base de 9 ft. ¿Cuál es la altura?
hintsEs: Esta vez te dan el área (54 pies²) y la base (9 pies): la altura es la pieza que falta.
Empieza con A = b × h. Para deshacer una multiplicación, divide: h = A ÷ b.
Escribe 54 = 9 × h y luego divide 54 entre 9 para hallar la altura en pies.

questions.stem: What is the area of a parallelogram with base 9 cm and height 5 cm?
choiceFeedback: Add base and height? The formula multiplies them.
22.5 is half of 45; is that the area formula?
hints: Spot the base (9 cm) and the height (5 cm). Which operation does the area formula use on them?
Use A = base × height. If your number looks like 9 + 5, or like half the product, rethink the operation.
Compute 9 × 5 and give the answer in square centimeters.
questions.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el área de un paralelogramo con base 9 cm y altura 5 cm?
hintsEs: Identifica la base (9 cm) y la altura (5 cm). ¿Qué operación usa la fórmula del área con ellas?
Usa A = base × altura. Si tu número se parece a 9 + 5, o a la mitad del producto, repiensa la operación.
Calcula 9 × 5 y da la respuesta en centímetros cuadrados.

reviewHighlights.watchOut: The most common mistake in Area of Parallelograms is multiplying the base by the slanted side instead of the perpendicular height. For a parallelogram with a base of 16 ft, a perpendicular height of 9 ft, and a slanted side of 11 ft, students compute 16 × 11 = 176 square feet instead of the correct 16 × 9 = 144 square feet. The height must be the straight-up (perpendicular) distance between the base and its opposite side, not the length of the slanted side, even though the slanted side is often the number that 'looks' like it belongs in the formula.

level1.stem: Which measurement is the height of a parallelogram?
choices: The length of the slanted side
The perpendicular distance between the base and the opposite side
level1.explanation: The height is always the perpendicular (straight up-and-down) distance between the base and the opposite side, not the slanted side.
choiceFeedback: The slanted side is not perpendicular to the base.
Perimeter is around the shape; height is perpendicular distance.
The longest side is not always the height.
hints: Picture a leaning parallelogram. The height is not a side you can trace — it's a distance measured straight across.
Height must make a right angle (90°) with the base. Test each choice: is this perpendicular to the base?
Draw a base, then a straight up-and-down dashed line to the opposite side. That dashed line is what 'height' means here.
level1.stemEs: ¿Cuál medida es la altura de un paralelogramo?
level1.explanationEs: La altura siempre es la distancia perpendicular (recta, de arriba abajo) entre la base y el lado opuesto, no el lado inclinado.
choicesEs: La distancia perpendicular entre la base y el lado opuesto
hintsEs: Imagina un paralelogramo inclinado. La altura no es un lado que puedas trazar: es una distancia medida en línea recta.
La altura debe formar un ángulo recto (90°) con la base. Prueba cada opción: ¿es perpendicular a la base?
Dibuja una base y luego una línea punteada recta hacia arriba hasta el lado opuesto. Esa línea punteada es lo que significa 'altura' aquí.

level3.prompt: A parallelogram has a base of 12 cm. If you double the height, the area doubles too. Explain why this happens using the formula, and give a specific example with numbers.
level3.sentenceFrame: When the height doubles from ___ to ___, the area changes from ___ to ___ because in the formula A = b × h, the base stays at ___ and ___.
level3.hint: Pick a starting height; use A = base x height to see what happens.
hints: The base stays 12 cm the whole time — only the height changes. Your explanation should lean on A = b × h.
Pick an easy starting height (like 5 cm), find the area, then double the height to 10 cm and find the new area.
Compute 12 × 5, then 12 × 10. Describe what happened to the area when the height doubled, using the word 'multiply'.
level3.explanation: In A = b × h the base of 12 cm is a fixed factor, so the area is just 12 times whatever the height is. With h = 5, A = 12 × 5 = 60 sq cm; doubling to h = 10 gives A = 12 × 10 = 120 sq cm, exactly double, because doubling one factor doubles the product.
level3.explanationEs: En A = b × h la base de 12 cm es un factor fijo, así que el área es simplemente 12 veces la altura que tengas. Con h = 5, A = 12 × 5 = 60 sq cm; al duplicar a h = 10 queda A = 12 × 10 = 120 sq cm, exactamente el doble, porque duplicar un factor duplica el producto.
level3.promptEs: Un paralelogramo tiene una base de 12 cm. Si duplicas la altura, el área también se duplica. Explica por qué pasa esto usando la fórmula y da un ejemplo específico con números.
hintsEs: La base se queda en 12 cm todo el tiempo; solo cambia la altura. Tu explicación debe apoyarse en A = b × h.
Escoge una altura inicial fácil (como 5 cm), halla el área, luego duplica la altura a 10 cm y halla el área nueva.
Calcula 12 × 5 y luego 12 × 10. Describe qué le pasó al área cuando la altura se duplicó, usando la palabra 'multiplicar'.
